threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the new folks by how they stand awkwardly at the bus stop, staring at their phones like they’re waiting for a ride-share instead of the 394.
Caught a couple arguing about whether the Clapham Common statue is a 'honourable man' or 'a shady bloke'—only in Brixton at 2 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a spontaneous dance-off at Körnerpark on a rainy Tuesday, I knew this place was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar where the beer is served in a glass jar with a pink rubber duck floating on top. It's utterly bizarre but oddly charming.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they casually mention how the BART delays altered their dinner plans, not just their commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus while the driver tried to get everyone to stay seated. Classic SF chaos—makes you wonder who’s really keeping the show going.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think it’s all about the parks and plazas, but they miss the magic of wandering the narrow streets, where every corner holds a new, forgotten café.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to try the local bakeries, still clutching a box of dry pastries from that chain in the Eixample.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use the 'tube map' app instead of checking if the bus goes your way. Everyone knows the bus will probably get you there quicker.
Caught the 188 last night; overheard a couple arguing over which kebab shop was better. Turns out, it's a serious rivalry around here.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sipping coffee at 8 AM, the sound of a nearby street performer on Weserstrasse blasting a trumpet, while a cat lazily suns itself on a windowsill. Perfect Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not unusual to see people at the Spree river tossing back beers while casually jumping into the water—like it's just another day at the park.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows the exact time the burrito line at La Taqueria gets crazy—it's always at 12:30, right after the tech crowd descends.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, a saxophonist set up shop next to a broken Muni bus, playing soulful tunes while people waited. Only in SF can delays spark spontaneous concerts.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always flock to Park Güell but miss the hidden gardens around Vila de Gràcia, where locals unwind and escape the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still trying to order 'café con leche' without the accent, while fumbling with the metro map at Diagonal.
